**100** of 100

Every civil construction project runs on **formats** — the standard documents that contractors, site engineers, storekeepers, and developers fill in every single day. **BBS (Bar Bending Schedule)**, **GRN (Goods Received Note)**, **BOQ format**, **pour card**, **level book**, **performance bank guarantee**, **RERA QPR**, **bore log** — these are the operational backbone of an Indian construction site. InfraLens curates **100 site-ready formats** across 10 work-streams: tendering, site execution, stores, rate analysis, MEP testing & commissioning, statutory / NOC, RERA compliance, survey, geotechnical, and land acquisition. Each format is Excel + PDF, IS / IRC code-mapped where applicable, and free to download.

Show more ↓

## Why every Indian site needs a standard format library

Indian construction runs on paperwork — and the paperwork is **format-driven**. The contractor's site office prints stacks of GRNs, MIRs, bin cards, pour cards, BBS sheets every week. The PMC office tracks IPCs, FPCs, MOMs, and risk registers. The developer files RERA QPRs every quarter. The surveyor maintains traverse and level books from day one of site mobilization. Without standardised formats, you get inconsistency across sites, lost data between contractors, audit failures during ISO/RERA/NABL reviews, and disputes that drag on for years.

The **CPWD Works Manual 2019**, **MoRTH Specifications for Road & Bridge Works**, **FIDIC Conditions of Contract**, **IS 456**, **IS 1786**, **IS 383**, **RERA Act 2016**, and **BOCW Act 1996** all explicitly or implicitly require certain documents — IPCs per the contract, MTC verification per IS 1786, NCRs per ISO 9001, QPRs per RERA Section 11(1)(d). InfraLens **Formats** provides the operational documents themselves — pre-formatted, code-mapped, ready to print or fill in Excel.

**Three role-hubs on InfraLens:** [PMC Templates](https://infralens.in/pmc) is the consultant's toolkit (150 templates for site oversight). [QA/QC Templates](https://infralens.in/qaqc) is the quality engineer's toolkit (300+ checklists, test reports, ITPs). **Formats** is everything else — the contractor's, storekeeper's, surveyor's, developer's, MEP engineer's day-to-day documents. Together the three hubs cover the full lifecycle: tender → mobilise → execute → bill → quality-check → hand over.

## How the 100 formats are organised — 10 work-streams

**Tendering (18 formats)**: BOQ format (CPWD + PWD), PQ application, technical bid compliance, financial bid (item rate + percentage rate), EMD register, bid bond tracker, pre-bid query register, bid comparison statement, deviation sheets (tech + commercial), LOI/LOA templates, performance bank guarantee submission, mobilisation advance request, tender schedule, vendor empanelment.

**Site Execution (25 formats)**: Bar Bending Schedule (BBS) for beam / column / slab / footing / pile, level book, setting-out register, pour cards (column / beam / slab / raft), pour permit, concrete cube log, slump test log, daily pour register, site DPR, site WPR, brickwork / plaster / blockwork inspection, shuttering inspection, de-shuttering permit, reinforcement fixing inspection, formwork removal schedule, curing register.

**Stores (10 formats)**: GRN (Goods Received Note), Indent / MIR, issue voucher, material returns note, bin card, monthly reconciliation, cement consumption register, steel consumption register, stores inward register, dead stock register.

**Estimation & Rate Analysis (10 formats)**: Rate analysis for PCC, RCC M25, brickwork, plaster (internal + external), shuttering; labour productivity, plant productivity, overhead & profit computation, escalation calculation per price-adjustment formula.

**MEP Testing & Commissioning (10 formats)**: AHU commissioning, chiller commissioning, DG set load test, lift / elevator testing protocol, fire alarm (FAS) T&C, PA system T&C, LT panel schedule, cable schedule, earthing test register, IR (insulation resistance) test register.

**Statutory / NOC (8 formats)**: Building permit application (BPA) checklist, fire NOC, OC application, CC application, AERB license tracker, pollution NOC (CPCB / SPCB) tracker, factory license application, rain water harvesting compliance.

**RERA (6 formats)**: Quarterly Progress Report (QPR), Form 5 (Annual Audit), escrow account reconciliation, allotment letter, possession letter, customer ledger / demand letter.

**Survey (5 formats)**: Control point register, traverse register, total station reading sheet, DGPS observation log, cross-section format.

**Geotechnical (5 formats)**: Bore log, SPT test sheet, plate load test, CBR test sheet, lab test request form.

**Land Acquisition (3 formats)**: 3A/3D notification tracker (NHAI), LA Act Section 4(1)/6(1) notice register, R&R (Resettlement & Rehabilitation) compensation register.

## What's the right format for your role?

**Contractor's site office** — start with the **Site Execution** family (BBS, pour cards, daily reports) + **Stores** (GRN, bin card) + **Tendering** (BOQ formats for the next bid). Roughly 50 of the 100 formats are directly used by a contractor's site team.

**PMC / Consultant** — primarily use [PMC Templates](https://infralens.in/pmc) (MOMs, IPC certification, audit reports), but cross-reference **Tendering** formats during bid evaluation + **Statutory** trackers for compliance oversight.

**Developer / Real-estate** — **RERA** quarterly and annual filings + **Statutory** (BPA, OC, fire NOC) + selective **Site Execution** trackers from contractor.

**Surveyor** — **Survey** family from day 1 (control points, traverse, level book) + **Geotech** during initial soil investigation.

**MEP contractor** — **MEP T&C** family for system commissioning + **Stores** for material tracking + **Tendering** during bidding.

**Project manager** — uses all 10 work-streams selectively. The **Estimation** rate analysis sheets and **Tendering** BOQ formats are the most commercially valuable; the **Site Execution** \+ **Stores** formats are operational backbone.

Each format on InfraLens is downloadable as **Excel** (editable, with formulas where applicable) and **PDF** (print-ready). Most are 1-3 pages; the BOQ and rate analysis formats are tabular, ready for population. All formats are mapped to the relevant IS code, IRC code, FIDIC sub-clause, CPWD Works Manual chapter, or statutory Act / Rule wherever applicable.

## Frequently Asked Questions

10 common questions about this topic, answered by civil engineers.

What is a BBS (Bar Bending Schedule) and how do I prepare one?+

A **BBS** is a table listing every reinforcement bar in a concrete element — bar mark, diameter, shape, length, number of pieces, weight. It's the procurement document for steel and the issue document for steel-fixers. Prepare per **IS 2502:1963** (Code of Practice for Bending and Fixing of Bars). Columns: Bar Mark, Diameter (mm), Type / Shape Sketch, Length (mm), No. of Bars, Total Length (m), Unit Weight (kg/m per IS 1786 Table 3), Total Weight (kg). One BBS per element (footing, column, beam, slab) is standard; site uses it to cut + bend rebar before fixing. Total weight from BBS × wastage factor (~3-5%) = procurement quantity.

What is the difference between a GRN, MIR, and Issue Voucher?+

**GRN (Goods Received Note)** is filled when material arrives at site — it records the supplier, invoice number, quantity received, quality check status. The storekeeper signs the GRN to acknowledge receipt; the GRN is the basis for raising the bill. **MIR (Material Issue Request)** or **Indent** is filled by the site engineer requesting material from stores — element, quantity, date needed. The storekeeper checks bin card, issues against the MIR. **Issue Voucher** is the storekeeper's confirmation that material was actually issued to the requesting site engineer, with quantity, date, signature. These three documents — GRN, MIR, Issue Voucher — form the audit trail from supplier to site consumption.

What is RERA Form 5 and when is it filed?+

**RERA Form 5** is the **Annual Audit Report** that every promoter must file with the state RERA Authority within 6 months of the end of each financial year. It's a Chartered Accountant's certificate confirming that (a) 70% of amounts collected from allottees were deposited into the project-specific escrow account, (b) withdrawals were proportionate to the percentage of construction completion, (c) project finances are healthy. Required per **RERA Act 2016 Section 4(2)(l)(D)** and state RERA rules. Quarterly progress reports ( **QPRs**) are separate — they're filed every 3 months, covering work done, photos, money received, money spent, expected completion date. Both forms vary by state RERA; MahaRERA, RERA Karnataka, RERA Haryana each have slightly different templates.

What is a Performance Bank Guarantee and how is it tracked?+

A **Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG)** is a bank guarantee submitted by the contractor securing performance of the contract — typically **5-10% of contract value** per CPWD or **5% per FIDIC Red Book Sub-Clause 4.2**. Issued by a scheduled commercial bank, valid for the contract period + defects liability period (usually 12-24 months). The Performance BG Tracker format records: BG number, issuing bank, amount, validity from-to, project, contractor, status (live / extended / claimed / released). Common issues tracked: BG expiry (renewal needed 30 days before expiry), claim invocation (during disputes), release after DLP completion. Every contract has a separate PBG — the tracker maintains the portfolio for the PMC / developer.

What is a price adjustment / escalation formula?+

**Price Adjustment (PA)** or **Escalation** compensates the contractor for cost increases over a long-duration contract. The standard CPWD / MoRTH formula breaks the contract into components (cement, steel, bitumen, labour, fuel, others) each with a weightage and an indexed base + current price. Formula: PA = Contract Value × Σ (Weight × (Index\_Now − Index\_Base) / Index\_Base). Indices used: All India WPI for cement / steel (released monthly by Economic Advisor's office), Labour wage rate from CPWD Schedule, RBI fuel index. The Escalation Calculation format does this computation for each Running Account Bill — typically applied after 24 months from contract date or quarterly depending on contract terms. For DSR-based contracts, the analogous concept is **star rate** for new items not in the schedule.

What test is conducted with a plate load test?+

The **Plate Load Test (PLT)** is conducted per **IS 1888:1982** to determine the safe bearing capacity and settlement characteristics of soil at the foundation level. A steel plate (300mm × 300mm or 600mm × 600mm) is placed at the test depth, loaded incrementally (5 increments to design load + 50%), and settlement is measured at each increment. Output: load-settlement curve, ultimate bearing capacity (load at which curve becomes asymptotic), safe bearing capacity (ultimate / factor of safety, typically 2.5-3). Test is performed for important structures > 3 floors or wherever soil is variable; minimum 2-3 tests per building. The Plate Load Test format records the apparatus, load increments, settlement readings every 5-10 min until stable, and computed bearing capacity.

What is the LA Act 2013 Section 4(1) notice?+

Under the **Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013** (LA Act 2013, also called **RFCTLARR Act**), **Section 4(1)** is the preliminary notification that the government intends to acquire land for a public purpose. It triggers the Social Impact Assessment (SIA) under Section 4(2). After SIA, **Section 6(1)** is the declaration of acquisition. **Section 11** is the public notice + objections period. **Section 19** is the award (compensation determination). The LA Act notice register tracks each notification (3A under NHAI Act 1956 for highways, or Section 4(1) under RFCTLARR for general acquisition), dates, area notified, objections received, status. Each highway project from NHAI follows the **National Highways Act 1956 Sections 3A, 3D, 3G** (faster process for highways, ~1 year).

What is an IR (Insulation Resistance) test and how often is it done?+

**Insulation Resistance (IR) Test** checks the integrity of electrical cable insulation by applying a DC voltage (500V or 1000V depending on system voltage) between conductor and earth using a **megger** instrument. Per **IS 732:2019** (Code of Practice for Electrical Wiring Installations), the minimum acceptable IR value is **1 megohm** (for low-voltage systems up to 500V) or higher for HV systems. Test is conducted: (a) Before commissioning every new circuit, (b) After any modification, (c) Periodic preventive maintenance — typically annually for industrial, 5-yearly for residential. The IR Test Register records: circuit ID, cable size, voltage, megger reading at 1 minute, polarisation index (10-min reading / 1-min reading — > 2 is good), pass/fail, signed by electrical engineer.

Are these formats free to use commercially?+

Yes — all 100 InfraLens formats are free to download, free to edit, and free to use on commercial construction projects. There's no watermark, no licensing fee, no attribution requirement. Do these formats work for projects outside India?+

The **format structure** (table columns, sections, signoff blocks) is universally applicable to any civil construction project. The **specific code references** (IS, IRC, CPWD, RERA, BOCW) are India-specific. For projects using ASTM, BS, EN, or FIDIC-based contracts internationally, replace the IS code references with the contract-specified standards (e.g., "per IS 456" becomes "per ACI 318" or "per BS 8110"). The pour card, BBS, GRN, level book, traverse register, bore log, plate load test structures are independent of jurisdiction. Tendering formats (BOQ, IPC) follow CPWD format but the FIDIC-style equivalents are very similar. RERA formats are India-specific (no direct international equivalent).
